chapter: Theater broadcasts, recordings and the road
title: Houston's Rice Hotel and the rival trumpeter's polish
summary: He tells of a night on the Rice Hotel roof in Houston, being left to fill the job, and the can of metal polish.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: Yes, sir. They used to send out the orchestrations with two pieces, just like you say, a platter, with the flaps, what do you call it, the flap? What's the side they don't expect? The flip side. The flip side. They give you two pieces, one orchestration. So I put that on there. So if I went big, and I always went big, not to brag, I'd get up and I'd give them those three-fifths notes, and we'd go into it, knock them stiff. Easy. Easy. But maybe luck. Maybe just do good judgment. Maybe some inborn experience. I told this one, because Texas hadn't heard any jazz. The leader at the Rice Hotel, I knew him very well, his name was Finley. And the bassist was the same fella that I told you was the first man ever to... They invited me to play a night on the rice roof. The Rice Hotel was the center of Houston's nightlife. Well, the trumpet player, he got disgusted, I guess, and he thought he was outside, he went home and left me stuck with the job for the night. So I stayed there and played, and Finley asked me if his name was... Could I get plenty to join with me and come join his orchestra? Tony and I were doing something, you know, fairly, you know, didn't want to go. So this trumpet player said, Johnny, I want to thank you for filling out the night for me, I want to give you something. And he has me a can of metal polish. I had a brass trumpet at that time because, you know, I thought I could get a better tone out of it, and all I ever polished was the bell, because that's all the people could see. It was a miserable looking horn, but it was a great horn, I'm telling you, it was like another painted Stradivarius, it had it, you know what I mean?
